articles.title: Meta struck an unusual deal to keep Mark Zuckerberg from leaving California
articles.summary: Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg has made a deal with the firm's board allowing him to sell or transfer up to 20% of the company's new Class C stock so that his voting majority doesn't decrease even if he has to pay the billionaire tax. (Nic Coury / Associated Press ) Meta’s Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg has wielded enormous power over the social media empire he built more than two decades ago, leading the California juggernaut through major scandals, scrutiny and technological shifts. But the 42-year-old tech mogul considered leaving the state because he feared that a ballot measure to impose a one-time 5% tax on the assets of California billionaires could reduce the amount of control he has over Meta, a recent regulatory filing shows. Meta’s board struck a deal so he would stay in California. Meta is the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. The filing highlights how one of the world’s wealthiest people, whose net worth totals more than $200 billion, is bracing for the possibility that California voters pass Proposition 40, a wealth tax proposal that would primarily be used to fund healthcare. Although supporters say the fear that billionaires will flee the state are overblown, the ultrawealthy have made moves to potentially avoid paying the tax or are funding campaigns to defeat it. Read more: Your guide to Proposition 40: California's billionaire tax proposal Zuckerberg’s influence over Meta is partly tied to how the company structures its stock. Zuckerberg holds roughly 60% of voting power over Meta even though he only owns about 13% of the company’s total shares. Meta has a dual-class share structure, dividing the stock into Class A shares with one vote each and Class B shares with 10 votes each. Zuckerberg holds a large amount of Class B stock, which gives him majority control over company decisions. If the wealth tax proposal passes, Zuckerberg is worried that it could reduce his voting power, according to the filing. The tech executive makes an annual salary of $1, so most of his wealth is linked to his stake in Meta. If he had to sell his Class B shares to pay the tax, that would reduce his voting majority in the company, according to the filing. In September, he told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Palo Alto home for sale, pressuring board members to find a solution. On Wednesday, Meta announced a new class of stock with no voting rights called Class C that would take effect in January. As part of the deal, Zuckerberg could sell or transfer up to 20% of Class C stock so his voting majority doesn’t decrease even if he has to pay the tax. “Mr. Zuckerberg’s continued leadership role in our Company, and his continuing presence at the Company’s headquarters in California, is critical at this current inflection point for the Company and the tech industry in order to continue to provide value-maximization for all shareholders,” the filing said. Since the company’s public debut, its share price has risen more than 1,700%, outperforming the S&P 500. In Meta’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday, Chief Financial Officer Susan Li said creating a new class of nonvoting stock benefits the company in various ways, including “capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, other general corporate purposes.” “We believe this share class will maintain our founder-led structure. It will expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI,” she said. Meta has roughly 66,700 workers globally. Its sprawling headquarters is in Menlo Park. Some billionaires such as Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey, Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen and Google co-founder Sergey Brin have opposed the wealth tax proposal. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, on the other hand, has said he doesn’t mind paying more taxes. The Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West is backing the wealth tax proposal and says it applies to roughly 200 billionaires who have resided in California as of January 1, 2026, and could raise $100 billion. More than $300 million has been contributed to fight the billionaire tax, including two propositions that could block it if they gather more votes. Although stock prices fluctuate, Zuckerberg could face a tax liability of roughly $12 billion based on his net worth. In 2015, Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan, pledged to give away 99% of his Facebook shares over their lifetimes when they celebrated the birth of their first daughter. The couple created the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, a philanthropic organization whose efforts include curing, managing and preventing all diseases. Although Zuckerberg lives in Palo Alto, he also owns real estate elsewhere, including in Hawaii, Washington, D.C. and Ireland. Times data journalist Gabrielle LaMarr LeMee contributed to this report. articles.title: New York City approves ban on horse-drawn carriages. Phase-out set for 2028.
articles.summary: A New York tradition more than a century old is ending. The New York City Council on Oct. 22 voted to ban horse-drawn carriages , winding down a historic tradition that's popular among tourists and fiercely opposed by animal rights groups. In a 40-7 vote, the council approved a ban that will phase out the operation of horse carriages that are in and around Central Park by June 2028. "Today’s historic vote marks our commitment to animal welfare, public safety, and protecting workers," council speaker Julie Menin said in a statement. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani supports the bill and is expected to sign it into law. In early October, he declared that the horse carriage industry is "coming to an end in New York City." The city's horse carriages have traversed a loop in Central Park dating back to the 1800s. By the mid-20th century, the city limited horse-drawn carriage licenses to 68. Over the decades, the carriages became a tourism staple and appeared in iconic films and television shows, such as "Sex and the City," "Elf" and "Home Alone 2: Lost in New York." But in recent years, animal rights groups and others have increasingly called for the end to the tradition, arguing that the practice subjects horses to harsh unnatural conditions and physical exhaustion. Opposition mounted this summer following the death of 18-year-old Romanch Mahajan , an Indian tourist killed in June after being thrown from a horse carriage. The legislation phasing out the longstanding tradition is named after Mahajan, whose parents appeared at the Oct. 22 city council meeting. In June, a horse named Deniz collapsed suddenly in Central Park while pulling a carriage with passengers, setting off another wave of backlash against the horse-carriage industry. President Donald Trump , who is from New York, weighed in on the vote, criticizing the city council's decision and calling horse carriages a "great tradition" that "will be missed." "The Horse-drawn Carriage in New York City is a quintessential New York experience. So sad that, for political reasons, we will see it go!" he said in a post on Truth Social . Some who oppose the legislation say it does not adequately protect workers who rely on the carriages for their income. Officials say there are about 150 horse-carriage drivers currently working in the city. Outside City Hall, carriage driver Alexus Lawson, 28, called the vote a “travesty.” “New Yorkers want us,” she said, wearing a tie and a black top hat. “We’re not going down without a fight.” The union representing Lawson and over 100 other carriage drivers, the Transport Workers Union of America, has vowed to sue the city in an attempt to block the legislation from taking effect. "If the NYC Council bans horse-carriage rides, hundreds of blue-collar drivers, owners, and their family members will be financially ruined and emotionally devastated," the union previously said in a statement on X. The bill requires the mayor’s office to develop a transition plan by April 2027 and to consider a program to compensate carriage operators for their businesses and help with the disposition of their horses. Under the proposal, the horses could not be slaughtered. City Hall has promised that it is working toward a transition to help protect carriage workers. "We have been working closely with the City Council, union partners, carriage drivers, animal welfare advocates, and community leaders to deliver a just transition that protects workers while ending horse-drawn carriages in Central Park once and for all," City Hall spokesperson Sneha Choudhary previously told USA TODAY. New York City is the latest major metropolitan area that’s voted to ban horse-drawn carriages. Over the last five years, cities including Philadelphia, Chicago and San Antonio, have outlawed the practice. Contributing: Reuters Christopher Cann is a national reporter for USA TODAY. articles.title: DOJ investigating Corey Lewandowski's role in DHS contracting under Kristi Noem
articles.summary: Corey Lewandowski speaks to the press in July 2024..(Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images) - Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Justice Department prosecutors are investigating allegations of contract misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security, including the role of Corey Lewandowski who worked as de facto chief of staff to former Secretary Kristi Noem, according to multiple people familiar with the investigation. The probe follows a criminal referral for Lewandowski from the DHS Inspector General’s office, which has been examining contracting practices at the agency during Noem’s and Lewandowski’s tenure, according to one of the people familiar. The Justice Department declined to comment on the matter. “Mr. Lewandowski has not been contacted by the Justice Department regarding any investigation, and he denies any wrongdoing when he was proudly serving his country in a voluntary capacity,” Lewandowski’s attorney Adam Trigg told CNN. The Department of Homeland Security didn’t immediately return a request for comment on the matter. The referral is an unusual move for the Trump administration, which has been hesitant to criminally investigate its own members. Critics have instead largely accused the Justice Department of improperly targeting the president’s political enemies and accused DHS of protecting their own employees from scrutiny. In recent months, as the allegations of possible corruption emerged, Washington, DC, US Attorney Jeanine Pirro told officials in her office that she wanted investigators to look into claims of kickbacks connected to contracting at DHS, according to a second source familiar with the investigation. It’s still not clear which US Attorney’s office is leading the investigation. Prosecutors have been awaiting results from the DHS inspector general probe, the person familiar with the probe said. Lewandowski, a Republican operative, became a fixture at DHS early in President Donald Trump’s second term, serving as Noem’s chief adviser. But on paper, he was originally tapped to serve as a special government employee — a unique role meant to span a limited number of days. Lewandowksi’s straddling of senior government functions at DHS and service as a special government employee was uncharted territory, according to multiple people who spoke with CNN. Homeland Security officials ultimately viewed Lewandowski, a Trump ally, as Noem’s gatekeeper. He left the department when Trump fired Noem. Noem’s handling of contracts within DHS was one of the main catalysts for her ouster by Trump earlier this year, notably when she claimed that Trump knew of a $220 million ad campaign prominently featuring the secretary. During her tenure, Noem also tightened her grip on her department’s purse strings, ordering that every contract and grant over $100,000 had to cross her desk for approval — a move that Noem frequently defended as intended to cut down on waste but that multiple Homeland Security officials found unusual and unnecessary. The inspector general, Joseph Cuffari, complained to Congress in early March that Homeland Security leadership had been obstructing some of his work. Trump, when asked by a reporter on Thursday about the Lewandowski investigation, said he didn’t know much about it as he only just learned of it. He repeatedly said, however, that if people working for him are dishonest, he wants them prosecuted. “They’re stealing from me, so I want my people to be honest,” Trump said. “And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do.” This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy's $4 million attack ad against Amy Acton divides Ohio Republicans
articles.summary: A new campaign ad in which the estranged mother of Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton argues that her daughter should not be elected as the Buckeye State's next governor has added a new level of controversy to what was already one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. Acton, a Democrat, is running to replace outgoing Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. She's facing Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a billionaire who ran an unsuccessful presidential campaign in 2024. In the ad, Acton's mother, Donna Arthur , calls her daughter a "liar" and urges Ohioans not to support her. "Don't let her become your governor," she says. "If you think she'll make your life better, you're fooling yourself. It will only get worse." As the ad began to spread across social media, Acton's brother released a statement in which he accused Arthur of siding with their stepfather after he was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was a child, and criticized Ramaswamy for attempting to use the alleged abuse as a "political talking point." Ramaswamy defended the ad on Tuesday, telling reporters that Acton's account of her past "does deserve to be scrutinized." His campaign confirmed to the Enquirer that it will spend $4 million to air the ad across the state. The ongoing controversy over the ad, which has been widely condemned by Democrats and sparked pushback from some Republicans, has put a new spotlight on the race for Ohio's top elected office. Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, an incumbent Republican locked in a tight reelection race, released a statement saying he personally "would not have run" the ad. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance, himself a former senator from Ohio, said Republicans who disapprove of the ad should " stop whining " and remember that politics is a "tough business" during a campaign stop in Cincinnati on Wednesday. DeWine, who has endorsed Ramaswamy in the race, made his first public comments on the ad on Thursday, telling reporters that it was "wrong." "The ad, on its face, is deeply, deeply troubling, but when you know the rest of the story … it just makes it more wrong," he said. "It's wrong to run this ad." Trump weighed in on the controversy on Thursday, praising Arthur for her “courage.” “What she was really doing was saving Ohio from making a truly horrible choice!” He wrote on Truth Social. “The Press is trying to convince everyone that this Ad is bad, because it’s so good! Who wouldn’t use such an Ad? I would, it’s called, ‘hitting pay dirt.’” Yahoo Once a key swing state, Ohio has steadily become redder in recent decades. Four years ago, DeWine won reelection by more than 25 percentage points . But polls suggest that Acton has a chance to break the GOP's long run of control over the Ohio Statehouse. Here's what you need to know about who she is, how her past informs what she stands for today and what the polls say about her chances of winning. Who is Amy Acton? Acton has been open about the "difficult" childhood she endured growing up in Youngstown, Ohio, in the 1970s. On her campaign website, she says she overcame "periods of abuse, hunger, and neglect, and even wound up living in a tent in the middle of winter." In 2019, she publicly alleged for the first time that she had been sexually assaulted by her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, between the ages of 9 and 12. After Acton's biological father reported the alleged abuse in 1978, Arthur was arrested and charged with rape, according to contemporary news reports and court documents obtained by the Associated Press . Acton's mother sided with her stepfather, disputing the allegations. The couple left the state before Arthur could face trial and reportedly remained together until his death in 2004 . Both Acton and her mother say they have not seen or spoken to each other since a court hearing in which Acton testified against her stepfather nearly 50 years ago. "In the courthouse after they were charged, I went to give her a kiss, and she just turned her cheek away. That was the last time I ever saw her," Acton told the now-shuttered newspaper the Vindicator in 2019. Acton found more stability after moving in with her father and became a standout student in high school. She earned a bachelor's degree from Youngstown State University and a medical degree from the Northeast Ohio School of Medicine, working various jobs to pay her way through college. She completed residencies in pediatrics and preventive medicine before becoming a professor at Ohio State University , where she taught classes on maternal and child health. She also directed a community organization called Project L.O.V.E. to promote preventive health care among Columbus-area children. In 2019, DeWine tapped her to become director of the Ohio Department of Health. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit a year later, she advised DeWine to take swift action to control the spread of the virus. Under her guidance, Ohio became the first state in the nation to shut down all public schools. Acton also gained national attention thanks to the daily public briefings she gave throughout the early stages of the pandemic. In May 2020, an opinion piece in the New York Times called her "The Leader We Wish We All Had." Acton resigned a month later amid pressure from the Republican-led state legislature to sign orders rolling back COVID restrictions, moves she would later say "there was no science for." She briefly remained part of DeWine's administration as a public health adviser before leaving to resume working in the nonprofit sector. She announced her plans to run for governor in early 2025 and cruised through the Democratic primary in May. Acton was married to her first husband, with whom she had three children, for nearly 20 years before they divorced in 2008. She married her current husband in 2010 and became stepmother to his three children. What does Acton stand for? As a Democrat running in a conservative-leaning state, Acton fits firmly into the moderate wing of her party. Her policy platform focuses heavily on affordability, including proposals to lower the cost of health care, combat fraud, cut high energy bills and crack down on corporations that take advantage of workers and consumers. In July, she drew criticism from some progressive Democrats for saying that she supported barring transgender children from participating in girls' and women's sports. Soon afterward, she added language to her website pledging to protect Ohio's LGBTQ community, without directly contradicting her previously stated stance on transgender athletes' participation in sports. Acton has also spoken in favor of Ohio's voter ID requirements, a position that puts her at odds with many Democrats who view such laws as a voter suppression tactic by Republicans. Acton has also called for an increase in funding for police departments, more money for public schools and heavy investment in Ohio's rural and farming communities. What are her chances? Polling in the Ohio governor's race has fluctuated significantly as Election Day has grown closer. In the aggregate, the polls suggest that Acton has steadily widened her lead over Ramaswamy over the past several weeks. At the same time, two polls released in October show Ramaswamy ahead. The Cook Political Report and the Center for Politics , two of the country's top nonpartisan forecasters, list the race as a toss-up. No polls of the race have been conducted since the ad featuring Acton's mother became public, so it's too early to gauge what impact — if any — the controversy might have on voters' views of the two candidates. articles.title: Holiday hiring is heating up: Retailers and shipping firms are looking for workers
articles.summary: Holiday hiring is heating up with multiple companies saying they are adding temporary workers in the coming months, ahead of the holiday shopping season. Amazon announced it is looking to fill 300,000 seasonal part-time and full-time roles across their national support operations during the holidays -- an increase of 50,000 positions compared to the same period in 2025. Seasonal employees will earn an average rate of about $20 an hour. Shipping company UPS said it will hire 100,000 workers in the next few months, noting that many applicants can get a job offer in less than 7 minutes. John Minchillo/AP - PHOTO: A UPS employee unloads a truck before making deliveries, June 29, 2023, in New York. Spirit Halloween, the largest Halloween retailer in the U.S., said it plans to employ a record 52,000 associates at store locations. Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images - PHOTO: The "Jack The Reaper" logo displayed in the windows of a Spirit Halloween seasonal holiday store in the location, August 26, 2024 in Los Angeles. Poultry company Butterball , famous for their turkey hotline, also said they are hiring their largest team on record to handle calls coming into their "Turkey Talk-Line" ahead of Thanksgiving. Hiring in September grew much less than expected, jobs report shows The October jobs report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics will be released in November but data released in September shows that hiring has been increasing, although not as much as economists expected. Approximately 29,000 jobs were added in September, down from the 162,000 projected the month prior. Inflation has also been top of mind for concerned shoppers as unemployment sits at 4.2%. Teen summer jobs hit historic lows as fewer employers hire seasonal workers According to Indeed Hiring Lab , seasonal postings are up 10%, more than this time last year, but job postings for roles in physical stores have also declined. Retail job postings have gone up 61%, Indeed said, but other roles are also available with loading and stocking jobs up 9%, sales roles increasing 8% and customer service positions rising 6%, as shoppers continue to purchase items online. articles.title: Karoline Leavitt offers blunt assessment of successor who lasted just 5 days
articles.summary: Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt acknowledged Thursday that her successor Katie Zacharia, who stepped down after less than a week as press secretary, was not a good fit for the job. “Look, White House press secretary is a tough job. I know that because I did it,” Leavitt said in an interview with Fox News Digital. “Many people say it’s one of the hardest jobs in politics. It takes a lot of preparation. Sometimes you don’t know how someone will perform until they go out there,” she continued. “As the president said, we wish Katie the best. The job obviously was not for her.” Leavitt said Trump is continuing his search for potential candidates, and she has offered to assist the president in finding a replacement. “I do obviously talk to him about what the job entails, and he knows it very well. Nobody understands the press better than Donald Trump. He knows that he needs someone who is tough, who is smart, who understands his policies, who is loyal and can go out there and put up a fight,” she said. Leavitt served as press secretary from the beginning of the second Trump administration in January 2025 until this August, saying she wanted to spend more time with her family. Prior to serving as White House press secretary, Leavitt worked as press secretary on Trump's 2024 presidential campaign. Despite her exit from the White House, Leavitt is still seen as a close confidant of Trump's. Leavitt’s comments came after Zacharia left the role after only five days on the job earlier this month. articles.title: Judge orders Trump to sit for deposition in BBC defamation lawsuit by Dec. 11
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — A federal judge on Thursday ordered President Donald Trump to sit for a deposition in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC by Dec. 11. The order from U.S. Magistrate Judge Enjoliqué Lett came as lawyers for the British broadcaster complained that Trump had delayed his appearance in his own lawsuit. Charles Tobin, attorney for the BBC , said that with two months left in the discovery period, “we still haven’t been able to depose the plaintiff.” Meanwhile, it remained uncertain whether former special counsel Jack Smith would be allowed to sit for a deposition. Federal rules require current and former employees to receive permission from agency heads before testifying in court cases. Smith has requested permission but has not received an answer, and the judge ruled that the department must respond to him by Nov. 2. In arguments about Trump's deposition, Tobin noted there had been an agreed-upon date of Oct. 16, but Trump had canceled it for a “matter of national importance.” He said the Republican president was in fact campaigning in Georgia that day. “He was participating in party politics and prioritized that over sitting for the deposition,” Tobin said. Lett said Trump must sit for a deposition by Dec. 11, or face sanctions up to dismissal of his lawsuit — unless the discovery period is extended by the presiding judge. Discovery, where lawyers for both sides exchange documents and other evidence, is scheduled to end Dec. 18, and the BBC's attorneys want to make sure they have Trump’s deposition before that deadline. Lett said only the presiding judge assigned to the case can alter the trial schedule, and the defense said it would be open to scheduling the deposition at a later time if the trial schedule was also changed. Trump, who has often avoided depositions, filed his lawsuit against the BBC last December . He accused the publicly funded broadcaster of defamation as well as deceptive and unfair trade practices related to a documentary, “Trump: A Second Chance.” The BBC acknowledged that filmmakers spliced together quotes from different sections of the speech Trump delivered to his supporters on Jan. 6, 2021 , before the storming of the U.S. Capitol, to make it seem he was directly urging violence. The broadcaster apologized over the editing , and the head of the BBC and its top news executive both resigned. But the BBC has denied Trump’s claims that it defamed him. Trump's attorneys also argued against recording his deposition on video, asking for only a court reporter. The judge ruled that the deposition could be recorded on video but only for attorneys, meaning it wouldn’t be released to the public. It remained unclear whether Jack Smith would be allowed to sit for deposition To bolster its defense, the broadcaster subpoenaed former special counsel Jack Smith earlier this month. Trump’s lawyers have argued that there is no good reason for Smith, who is not a party to the case, to appear. The BBC has said Smith has extensive knowledge of what happened that day. At issue in Thursday's hearing, though, was whether Smith had received the legally required permission from the Department of Justice. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Feeley told the judge that Smith had sent a letter to the department saying he would not testify without permission, and the agency had not yet responded. Lett ordered the department to respond to Smith by Nov. 2. It seems unlikely that the department would grant Smith permission, or that he would move forward without it. Earlier in the hearing, Tobin, the BBC lawyer, argued that Smith has not objected to being deposed for this case, meaning the only objection is coming from Trump. Tobin said the BBC is not trying to relitigate the events of Jan. 6, but Smith is one of the leading experts in what happened that day, and his deposition could lead the BBC to evidence that could help their case. “We can argue later on whether his testimony is admissible," Tobin said, “but we are entitled to that deposition.” Trump's lawyer, Alejandro Brito, said Smith has no personal knowledge of Trump’s Jan. 6 speech or Trump's state of mind when he gave it. All of Smith’s knowledge about the case is secondhand, Brito argued, and the special counsel's report, along with Smith’s testimony before Congress, is all public and available to the BBC’s attorneys. Judge says the BBC can see membership records for Mar-a-Lago The judge agreed that the BBC should be allowed to see records for the total number of applications for membership at Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida from Jan. 6, 2020, through Jan. 6, 2026, as well as the total cost of membership and initiation fees for new applicants. Tobin said one aspect of any defamation case is showing actual damages, and the popularity of Mar-a-Lago is a significant indicator of Trump’s reputation. The BBC's lawyer described the private club as “a place where he exhibits his reputation in front of people who are important to him.” Brito argued that Trump does not actually run Mar-a-Lago, and that his reputation is not associated with the club. articles.title: Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas charged with drug trafficking and money laundering
articles.summary: NORFOLK, Va. (AP) — Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas, one of the state’s most powerful Democrats, was charged Thursday with leading what authorities alleged was a wide-ranging criminal enterprise that acquired and distributed large quantities of marijuana and laundered the proceeds. Lucas, who has been in elected office for decades, used her political power to insulate the operation from scrutiny, according to an indictment charging her and six other defendants, including several of her relatives. She “put her own financial interests before the people she was elected to serve,” said U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche , who spoke at a news conference with FBI Director Kash Patel . Lucas surrendered, the Justice Department said. She made a brief appearance in federal court in Norfolk on Thursday afternoon, where she was released on her own recognizance, according to court records. She left the court without addressing journalists who shouted questions her way and went straight into a waiting vehicle. The charges, including drug trafficking and money laundering, came after the FBI searched Lucas' hometown office and a cannabis shop in which she has a stake in May. At the time of the search, Lucas — who has been a vocal critic of Republican President Donald Trump’s administration — characterized it as an attempt to intimidate her. Lucas says she won't be bullied by the federal government A statement attributed to Lucas posted on her social media account did not directly address the substance of the charges but said Thursday's actions amounted to the federal government wielding its “full weight” against a great-grandmother. “I will not be intimidated. I will not be bullied. And I will not back down,” Lucas said in the statement. Her attorney at the hearing declined comment outside. The brash 82-year-old lawmaker has spent decades ascending the ranks of Virginia politics and has served since 1992 in the state Senate, where she's the president pro tempore, overseeing the chamber in the lieutenant governor’s absence. More significantly, she leads the powerful Senate finance committee, through which all legislation with any budget impact must flow. She’s used the position to kill legislation she opposes. Justice Department denies politics played a role The indictment comes as Trump’s Justice Department has faced intense scrutiny over investigations and prosecutions against foes of the president that critics have called politically motivated. Blanche rejected any suggestion politics played a role in Lucas’ case, noting the investigation began well before the second Trump administration started in January 2025. “We don’t do political paybacks,” Blanche told reporters. A person familiar with the May search told The Associated Press at the time that the probe was opened during Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration. The person spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss a continuing criminal investigation. FBI alleges a ‘criminal marijuana enterprise’ Patel said in a statement that “Lucas and a close-knit group of family members and associates orchestrated a multi-year scheme to enrich their own criminal marijuana enterprise, ‘the Lucas Enterprise’ — using Lucas’ position as Chairwoman of the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee to insulate the enterprise from criminal scrutiny and influencing legislation to financially benefit themselves.” The indictment describes Lucas as the “leader of the enterprise” who “approved and directed criminal activities,” including arranging for the acquisition and distribution of marijuana and supervising the laundering of the proceeds. The indictment alleges Lucas worked this year with another of the defendants to use her political position to obtain a recreational marijuana license for him, with the understanding that the proceeds from sales under the license would be shared with her to support the “enterprise.” Since 2021, marijuana has been legal to possess in Virginia, and many shops across the state have sold cannabis-derived products. But full recreational sales are not yet underway; legislation enacted earlier this year will allow them beginning in July 2027. Law enforcement made multiple controlled purchases of marijuana from Lucas' shop, which purported to sell hemp products, in 2024 and 2025, the indictment said. In addition to drug and money laundering charges, Lucas faces charges of racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to commit honest services fraud and maintaining a drug-involved premises. An arraignment is scheduled for next month. Among the other defendants who face a mix of those and other charges are two daughters, Lisa Lucas Burke and Theresa Lucas-Lamb, and a grandson, Ryan Eichelberger. All three also made brief court appearances and were released on their recognizance, according to court records. Attorneys for Lucas-Lamb and Eichelberger declined comment; Andrew Sacks, who was listed in court records as an attorney for Burke, didn't respond to requests for comment. Attorneys for two other defendants who are not family members declined comment; a third who was also released Thursday had no attorney listed in court records. Virginia officials react A forceful advocate of legalizing marijuana, Lucas partnered in opening the shop, The Cannabis Outlet, in 2021. She has publicly spoken about her ownership stake as recently as June, though her most recent financial disclosure forms do not list the business by name. At the time of the search — when marijuana was recovered at The Cannabis Outlet, according to the indictment — many Democrats spoke up to defend Lucas. On Thursday, Scott Surovell, the Democratic leader of the state Senate, said in a statement that the indictment contained “serious allegations” but emphasized that “Senator Lucas has the right to defend herself, and she has my full support as she does so.” Attorney General Jay Jones, a Democrat who is close with Lucas, said the allegations against her must be tested in a “full and fair” legal process. House Speaker Don Scott, Lt. Gov. Ghazala Hashmi, and Gov. Abigail Spanberger, all Democrats, echoed those sentiments, with Spanberger adding that the timing of the indictment so close to the midterm election would “further erode” Americans' trust in the Justice Department. Lucas herself is not on the ballot this year. Ryan McDougle, the Senate Republican leader, said he would not comment while the court proceedings play out. The senator draws comparisons to Trump Lucas, who represents a district that includes her hometown of coastal Portsmouth, operates with a sometimes-profane, unapologetic style that’s drawn comparisons to Trump. She amassed a six-figure following on X and national attention, using the social media platform to advocate forcefully for her priorities and to bash her critics, including former GOP Gov. Glenn Youngkin. She’s also occasionally blasted members of her own party, including Spanberger, with whom she’s had disagreements. Earlier this year, Lucas helped lead Democrats’ ultimately unsuccessful plan to gerrymander the blue-leaning state’s congressional districts into a map intended to elect 10 Democrats and only one Republican. Along the way, she posted quips about four GOP members the intended map sought to oust, joking that they soon would be working at McDonald’s. She and other Democrats defended the maps as a reasonable response to Trump-backed efforts to boost the GOP’s midterm advantage in other states. Lucas has been in politics for decades Lucas has notched several historic firsts in her career. According to a biography from the state library, in 1971 she became the Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s first female shipfitter, a physically demanding job that involves working on metal assemblies for vessels. She launched her political career in 1984, when, the biography said, she became the first Black woman elected to the Portsmouth city council. After Democrats flipped control of the Senate in 2019, her peers elected her to serve as president pro tempore. And in 2024, she was tapped to lead the chamber’s budget committee. ___ Rankin reported from Richmond. Associated Press journalists Eric Tucker in Washington and Steve Helber in Norfolk contributed to this report. articles.title: Iran says 7 oil tankers attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as fears grow of a return to war
articles.summary: TEL AVIV, Israel (AP) — Seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz overnight after being hit by Iran or striking naval mines, Tehran said Thursday, a markedly high number as tensions rise over concerns about a return to all-out war . With days before a close election in Israel in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could lose power, and before next month’s U.S. midterm election in which war-linked high prices have sparked voter anger, there are concerns that U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran could resume. “Netanyahu wants to attack Iran, that’s not even a question,” Danny Citrinowicz, a researcher at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies and a former Iran specialist in Israel’s military and intelligence services, told The Associated Press. He accused Israel of rushing into another round with Iran without revamping its strategy. A clear Netanyahu victory in the Oct. 27 election means an attack is almost guaranteed, he said. Main opposition candidates are likely to focus on domestic issues first, but Citrinowicz said he believed the region is on the way toward "another kinetic escalation.” Iran repeats threat to attack U.S. bases in the region Iranian state television reported the claims about the latest attacks on ships, which the AP couldn't independently confirm. The report cited the Revolutionary Guard Corps navy, which again threatened to strike U.S. military bases in the region if the U.S. keeps helping to guide commercial ships through the strait. The report didn't mention casualties. Iran still asserts control over the waterway, a central point of leverage in any talks with the U.S. over the war. October has had the most reported attacks on commercial shipping since March in the war's opening weeks, according to a British military monitor, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations. UKMTO didn't report the latest attacks, but it has noted new reluctance by some shippers to report incidents. Oil producers have found ways to keep crude flowing , experts say, but at a mounting cost. Tankers continue moving through Strait of Hormuz despite attacks Oil tankers are still moving oil through the strait under U.S. military protection despite the recent upsurge in attacks, according to shipping data and analysis company Lloyd’s List Intelligence. Tanker operators willing to risk the voyage have been shuttling oil from Gulf producers through the strait at night with their location systems and mobile phones turned off using a U.S.-protected lane near the coast of Oman. Those tankers transfer oil to other tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman for shipment to customers in Asia. Those “active Gulf operators show little sign of retreating” despite 28 attacks on ships in October, the highest since the start of the war, Lloyd’s said in an online webinar Thursday. The so-called “dark shuttle” overseen by U.S. Central Command has helped return oil shipments from the Gulf at roughly prewar levels, but at high costs in time, money and sailors' lives. Spot charter rates for tankers have soared into the hundreds of thousands of dollars a day, while the ship-to-ship transfers can take several days. UN urges US and Iran to return to diplomacy to end conflict, reopen strait U.N. spokesman Stephane Dujarric said no commercial ships should be attacked and called for diplomacy between the U.S. and Iran to reopen the strait. “For the sake of the people of the region and for the broader world, we need to see that waterway reopen, and we need to see tensions go down," he told reporters Thursday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday said Tehran remains open to diplomacy, but is ready to defend itself. Iran has warned that it learned important military lessons from the war that began with U.S. and Israeli attacks on Feb. 28, indicating in recent days that it could expand targets to include infrastructure such as undersea cables and data centers. The United States, for its part, is sending more military assets to the region, including a third aircraft carrier and thousands of troops, to join the largest force of American warships and aircraft in the Middle East in decades. Mediators, meanwhile, have been trying to bring Washington and Tehran back to formal talks. Iran still promotes its latest proposal to end the war and fully open the strait within a week if the U.S. meets several conditions, including ending the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. It echoes conditions in the deal that fell apart within days of both sides signing it in June. U.S. President Donald Trump rejected the latest proposal last month, but both sides acknowledged that indirect discussions have continued. The stakes are even higher if all-out war resumes A return to full fighting would again endanger civilians throughout the region and complicate global deliveries of oil, natural gas and related products like fertilizer from the region and likely bring another spike in prices. The head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, this week acknowledged that the Islamic Republic will suffer under a prolonged U.S. blockade. But economic pain and strategic collapse are not the same thing, he added, according to Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency. Now the conflict has widened with the recent surge in fighting between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia. The Saudi kingdom backs a coalition of forces with Yemen’s internationally recognized government that is fighting the rebels. The Houthis' repeated deadly attacks on airports and other facilities inside Saudi Arabia have pressured the close U.S. ally, which has sought military aid. The escalation also has threatened a crucial shipping corridor, the Bab el-Mandeb at the southern end of the Red Sea. Meanwhile, the president of Saudi oil company Aramco, whose sites have been targeted by the Houthis, said the amount of oil moving through a pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz has increased threefold in light of the global energy crisis. The East-West pipeline’s capacity has surged from two million to seven million barrels each day, Amin Nasser said in an interview with Saudi-owned television Al Arabiya Business. He said the company has been using drones to assess any damage to the pipeline and help with firefighting. 点评：此次PHP（Personal Home Page，支撑全球大量网站和Web应用的开源脚本语言，全球范围内估计有约70%的网站依赖其运行）严重漏洞是在隐匿十余年后，借助OpenAI和谷歌的AI模型被揭露的，这再度凸显了AI安全的重要性。AI让攻击更容易，也让防御必须升级。IDC预计，2026年全球网络安全支出约3080亿美元，到2029年约4300亿美元。 2、 人形机器人 | 据上证报报道，具身智能，正从实验室走向应用场景。在广东，会自己找位绑钢筋的机器人、贴着高楼外墙行走的清洗机器人，已悄然“上岗”。机器人进了工地，订单就跟着来了。广州某建筑机器人企业产线负责人表示，目前量产的六款机器人里，几乎款款都有订单在手，排期排到12月份，依然满足不了客户需求。另外，特斯拉首席执行官埃隆·马斯克透露，计划为旗下擎天柱(Optimus)人形机器人建造一座"机器人学校"，保障人工智能训练顺利开展。同时表示，公司达成年产100万台机器人的目标，所需时间可能超过一年。 点评：华创证券认为，特斯拉此次释放Optimus量产超预期信号，产品技术路线逐步明晰，量产迈出关键一步，叠加后续催化密集落地，行业有望迎来新一轮行情。 3、 有色 · 钨 | 据上证报报道，10月22日，百川盈孚数据显示，钨产业链中间产品的仲钨酸铵、钨酸钠分别报价48万元/吨、44万元/吨，较21日分别上涨4.35%、2.33%。 点评：国金证券认为，供给端看，国内开采总量控制约束持续增强，钨精矿供给整体收缩，据中国有色金属工业协会数据，2026年上半年国内钨精矿产量为5.37万吨，同比下滑14.75%；海外目前仅有巴库塔钨矿、Sangdong矿、Dolphin矿能形成实际增量供给，供给弹性亦有限。需求端，AI引领新增长，传统需求焕新生。2025年国内钨需求合计约7.57万金属吨，同比增长5%；2026年上半年国内钨消费3.85万吨，同比增长7.3%。中期需求稳步抬升叠加供给约束延续，海外战略备库升级背景下，钨价格中枢有望继续上移。 4、 智能眼镜/MR头显 | 据中证报报道，根据TrendForce集邦咨询最新《2026近眼显示市场趋势与技术分析》，AR眼镜逐步由概念验证走向消费市场，Meta Ray-Ban Display Glasses展现超乎市场预期的成长动能，不仅提升消费者对AR眼镜的关注，也带动品牌与供应链加快产品布局。受益于Meta产品带动的外溢效应，其余AR眼镜品牌亦积极拓展产品线与销售市场，趁着其他科技巨头尚未全面入局，承接消费者对AR眼镜的尝鲜需求。TrendForce集邦咨询预估，全球AR眼镜出货量将由2025年的62万台跃升至2026年131万台，年增长率达111.1%。 点评：近年来AR眼镜产业快速增长，主要得益于三大核心驱动力：一是硬件成本大幅下降，入门级AR眼镜成本较2023年下降42%，主流产品价格降至两三千元；二是AI大模型赋能，使语音交互、实时翻译等高频场景体验大幅提升，推动产品从“显示终端”向“随身智能体”演进；三是科技巨头密集入局，加速了产业链成熟与应用生态构建。未来，随着技术不断迭代和生态完善，AR眼镜有望成为继智能手机之后的下一代重要计算平台。 5、 职业教育 | 据中证报报道，《世界职业技术教育标准框架》（《北京协议》）近日在2026年世界职业技术教育发展大会上由45个国家共同发布。协议将推动经济繁荣与社会进步、服务人的全面发展、拓宽社会公平通道、深化职业技能互学互鉴、积极应对未来挑战作为职业教育共同的价值追求；倡议完善职业学校办学体系、构建全民终身教育培训体系、产教协同建设教材、校企合作打造教师队伍、按岗位实际要求开展实习实训、人工智能赋能教育教学改革等育人体系；提出相应治理、保障、行动路径。《北京协议》是我国牵头推动研制形成的首个国际职业教育标准。 articles.title: Meta未来支出承诺飙至8250亿美元，信用风险指标创历史新高
articles.summary: Meta在人工智能基础设施上的资金承诺规模持续膨胀，正引发市场对其信用风险的高度关注。 据Meta周四在监管文件中披露，截至今年9月底， 公司已承诺的未来支出总额约达8250亿美元， 涵盖租约、云计算合同及数据中心等多类协议，其中大量资金与AI计算能力和基础设施建设直接相关。 这一数字较今年7月披露的约7000亿美元大幅攀升，短短数月内新增逾千亿美元承诺。 华尔街见闻提及 ，Meta Q3营收与Q4指引双超预期，公司上调了全年资本支出计划，并宣布新设一类无投票权股票，为未来的收购及其他支出提供潜在融资工具。周三美股盘后涨幅一度超过6.5%。 然而Meta第三季度自由现金流转负至负21.2亿美元，为公司2012年上市以来约14年中首次出现赤字，净利润亦大幅低于分析师预期。 周四美股收盘，Meta跌约7%，市值蒸发超1000亿美元。 衡量Meta信用风险的五年期信用违约互换（CDS）价格飙升至历史最高水平，公司债券相对于美国国债大幅走弱。 这反映出投资者的深层忧虑：科技巨头为AI扩张持续举债，将进一步加剧本已供过于求的债券市场压力。与此同时，Oracle、微软、博通等超大规模云计算商及芯片制造商的CDS价格也同步走高，显示市场对整个科技行业债务风险的警惕情绪在蔓延。 支出承诺规模从7000亿跳升至8250亿 本次市场波动的直接导火索，是Meta在季报后披露的最新支出承诺数据。根据公司于周四提交的监管文件，Meta已就各类租约和合同达成约8250亿美元的未来支出协议，其中大部分与人工智能算力及基础设施相关。 具体而言， Meta尚未计入资产负债表的经营性及融资性租约价值达3557亿美元，涵盖从今年剩余时间至2036年陆续生效的数据中心及能源基础设施租约。此外，截至9月30日，公司另有4545亿美元的不可撤销短期及长期合同，主要涉及第三方云算力采购、数据中心能源协议，以及旗下Reality Labs部门的消费硬件产品。 Meta还披露，公司承诺在五年内购买最高147亿美元的云计算容量，但该金额或因云服务商向其他客户出售容量而有所减少。 相比之下，Meta在今年7月披露的未来支出承诺规模约为7000亿美元，此番披露意味着承诺总额在短短数月内大幅跳升。 信用风险指标触及历史极值 据ICE Data Services数据 ，周四Meta五年期CDS价格单日最高上涨8.9个基点，升至约119.3个基点，创下该合约上市交易以来的盘中最高纪录。 CDS价格越高，意味着投资者为债务违约风险支付的保险成本越大，这一指标的跳升直接反映出市场对Meta债务负担的不安情绪。 市场新晋的"AI贝塔风向标"CoreWeave再度遭到重挫，其债券收益率重新升破15%。 超大规模云计算服务商的信用风险持续走高，相关股票亦开始引发投资者警觉。 巴克莱Andrew Keches报告指出，尽管Meta的股权层面公告"至少在孤立审视下必须被解读为正面"，但"14C文件中披露的评论似乎暗示着极为庞大的支出野心"，令其对此保持审慎。 Keches明确预期Meta将在近期发行债券，并指出"这将在一段时间内继续压制利差"。 与此同时，Meta现有债券相对于美国国债的息差也同步走阔，债券价格承压下行。Oracle、微软、博通等同类公司的CDS价格亦在当日随之攀升，表明此次市场的担忧情绪并不局限于Meta一家，而是蔓延至整个AI重度投资的科技板块。 扩张逻辑存在争议 值得关注的是，Meta的AI扩张路径与微软、Alphabet、亚马逊等竞争对手存在本质差异——Meta通常不对外出售算力，这意味着数据中心的过度投资风险将由公司自身完全承担，而非通过云服务客户加以分散。 在此前的季度财报电话会议上，投资者曾多次追问首席执行官马克·扎克伯格是否有开展云服务业务的具体计划，但扎克伯格并未给出明确答复。与此同时，Meta在季报中上调了全年资本支出预期，并宣布发行新一类无投票权股票，后者未来或可用于支付并购及其他费用。 目前，外界对于Meta能否从其庞大的AI投入中获得足够回报仍存疑虑，而不断攀升的支出承诺与信用风险指标，正促使债券市场投资者重新评估这场豪赌的代价。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 科技资本大举杀入好莱坞！马斯克被曝10亿美元入股Skydance，财务救援还是战略布局？
articles.summary: 马斯克被曝以约10亿美元入股Skydance，在为这家债务缠身的好莱坞巨头提供有限财务支撑的同时，也将全球最具影响力的科技富豪与好莱坞最大内容版图绑定在一起。 据Semafor率先报道，马斯克此次投资与Skydance其他投资者的增资同步进行，参与方包括董事会成员Laurene Powell Jobs。马斯克代表未回应置评请求，Skydance亦拒绝发表评论。消息公布后，Skydance股价盘中一度飙升7.5%至8.46美元，但随即触发熔断，恢复交易后一度跌至7.53美元，日内跌逾4.3%，最终收跌约1%。 这一先涨后跌的股价走势折射出市场的深层忧虑：面对Skydance近87亿美元的总债务，10亿美元的注资规模远低于市场此前预期，信用市场的压力信号并未因此解除。与此同时，马斯克持有CNN和CBS母公司股权所引发的编辑独立性争议，也令这笔投资的政治敏感性不亚于其财务意义。 交易背景：合并后的债务压力 Skydance于10月6日完成对华纳兄弟探索公司的收购，交易总价约1100亿美元，由此整合了派拉蒙、华纳兄弟两大电影厂牌，Paramount+与HBO Max两大流媒体平台，以及CNN、CBS等主要新闻和广播资产。 联席CEO David Ellison与Ynon Kreiz主导这场整合，公司承诺三年内实现60亿美元成本节约，并设定2029年底前将净杠杆率降至3.0倍的目标。 然而，合并完成后的资本结构令市场持续承压。 据报道，Skydance在交易融资中发行了创纪录的520亿美元债券，其中8年期次级留置权票据在发行当日即跌破面值至95美分附近，5年期信用违约互换（CDS）利差一度升至601个基点，超越2008年金融危机及雷曼兄弟破产时的历史峰值。 惠誉评级亦将原派拉蒙无担保债券置于约570亿美元新增有担保债务之后，原6.875%、2036年到期债券跌至77美分的历史低位。 按照粗略测算，此次收购融资的固定利率票据每年利息支出约33亿美元，加上约95亿美元浮动利率定期贷款，年度利息总负担约达40亿美元。马斯克的10亿美元，仅相当于约一个季度的利息覆盖。 规模落差：市场预期与现实的背离 此次投资的市场反应之所以如此剧烈，部分原因在于预期管理的失误。 就在消息公布前一天，本周三，亿万富翁媒体大亨John Malone在纽约Paley国际理事会峰会上公开预言马斯克即将入股，并将投资规模估计在80亿至100亿美元之间。 Malone援引Larry Ellison与马斯克之间的深厚渊源——Larry Ellison曾在2022年马斯克收购Twitter时投入10亿美元，并曾持有特斯拉股份、出任其董事会成员，同时个人担保了逾400亿美元的Skydance股权融资。 最终落地的10亿美元约为Malone预测下限的八分之一，相对于87亿美元总债务，占比仅略超1%。据ZeroHedge分析，信用市场对此的解读颇为直白：若公司需要向"家族友人"紧急募集股权，本身即是财务压力的信号，而非信心的背书。Fitch此前亦明确指出，仅靠60亿美元成本削减不足以实现去杠杆目标，公司还需通过增发股权或出售资产加以补充。 战略意图：X平台、xAI与内容版图的协同想象 尽管财务层面的贡献有限，马斯克此次入股的战略意涵却引发广泛关注。据彭博报道，马斯克此举将其与Larry Ellison的Oracle深度绑定——后者通过Oracle持有TikTok美国业务的股权，马斯克本人则掌控X平台。Skydance旗下现拥有电影、电视剧、体育直播及新闻等多元内容管线，与X平台在内容分发层面存在潜在协同空间。 马斯克旗下与SpaceX合并前名为xAI的AI公司需要高质量训练数据，亦使Skydance庞大的影视IP库具备额外价值。CNN和CBS的新闻内容、HBO的剧集资产，均可能成为AI模型训练的潜在数据来源。 然而，这一布局同样带来政治敏感性。马斯克与特朗普总统的密切关系，以及其对媒体自由言论的一贯立场，令CNN和CBS的编辑独立性问题再度成为焦点。David Ellison此前已公开表态，两家新闻机构将保持编辑独立，但据报道，消息确认后CNN内部已出现恐慌情绪。 好莱坞权力格局：科技资本的新一轮渗透 马斯克入股Skydance，是科技富豪持续渗透传统娱乐业的最新案例。此前，Larry Ellison通过个人担保深度介入Skydance的融资结构，Laurene Powell Jobs亦以董事会成员身份参与本轮增资。马斯克的加入，使这一资本联盟的科技属性进一步强化。 与其他科技富豪的娱乐业布局相比，马斯克此次入股的独特之处在于其与X平台和xAI的潜在协同，以及由此带来的内容分发与数据获取双重战略价值。但市场目前更关注的，是这笔投资能否真正缓解Skydance的债务压力。 articles.title: 报道：SK海力士放弃Solidigm美国IPO计划
articles.summary: 据韩国经济日报周五援引未具名业内人士报道，SK海力士已决定不再寻求旗下子公司Solidigm在美国进行首次公开募股（IPO）。 这一决定正值韩国监管部门加大对母子公司重复上市的审查之际。 韩国金融监督院院长李灿镇本月19日表示，Solidigm赴美上市可能涉及韩国重复上市监管规则；金融委员会主席李亿远22日也表示，Solidigm适用相关指引，SK海力士及其上层母公司需要履行保护股东权益的义务。 监管压力与股东权益争议升温 Solidigm源自SK海力士对英特尔NAND闪存及固态硬盘业务的收购。SK海力士于2021年完成相关业务整合，Solidigm目前重点布局面向人工智能数据中心的企业级固态硬盘（eSSD）。 此前，据媒体报道， Solidigm正考虑赴纳斯达克上市 ，时间可能最早在2027年，估值最高或达1500亿美元。上市融资有望为其扩充产能、研发投入提供资金，同时减轻SK海力士直接承担相关投资的压力。 但潜在上市也引发韩国市场对股东权益稀释的担忧。若Solidigm向外部投资者发行新股，SK海力士对其持股比例可能下降，未来也需要与外部股东分享部分利润。 SK海力士此前于10月1日表示，尚未就Solidigm的资本运作作出决定，公司正在评估内部资金与外部融资等方案，并强调任何决策都将以长期企业价值和股东利益为重要考量。此次放弃美国IPO的消息，意味着其融资安排可能出现调整，但公司尚未公开确认这一决定。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 多家公司，三季度净利环比增超50%
articles.summary: 10月22日晚间，沪深两市上市公司继续集中披露2026年三季度报告。据不完全统计，当日有10家公司第三季度归母净利润环比增超50%，其中行云科技环比增幅约655%，奥士康约470%，中富电路约303%，华正新材约341%，晶丰明源约230%，华盛昌约179%，同花顺约55%，凯莱英约53%，宏和科技约52%，山东玻纤约52%。 这些单季利润陡增的公司集中指向两条线索：PCB产业链上游基材的量价齐升，以及算力基础设施需求的规模化兑现。 PCB产业链量价齐升， 基材环节最为受益 PCB产业链是当晚环比高增公司最集中的板块，包括华正新材、宏和科技、中富电路、奥士康等4家公司。 从各公司公告的业绩变动原因看，上游基材环节的表述高度一致。华正新材在三季报中表示，业绩增长主要系覆铜板单价及销量上升，带动营业收入及毛利率增加；公司第三季度实现归母净利润6.27亿元，同比增长3044.60%，环比增长341%；前三季度归母净利润7.99亿元，同比增长1177.71%。 宏和科技将增长归因于电子布销售单价上涨、特种电子布销量占比增加，公司第三季度归母净利润3.64亿元，同比增长607.73%；前三季度同比增长435.63%。 中富电路在三季报中将增长归因于订单增长、生产规模扩大。奥士康第三季度归母净利润3.71亿元，环比增长470%，其前三季度归母净利润为4.54亿元。 芯片设计企业晶丰明源的情况略有特殊，公司在三季报中说明，剔除四川易冲后营业收入同比增长明显，叠加并购四川易冲影响，第三季度归母净利润1.65亿元，环比增长230%——并购并表与自身景气回暖在其单季高增中同时起作用。 重整公司业务重构， 算力收入单季兑现 环比增幅最大的行云科技，其业绩变化背后是业务的整体重构。公司三季报显示，2026年是行云科技完成破产重整、产业投资人正式接管公司后的首个完整会计年度，业务模式较上年发生重大变化；公司确立跨境数字贸易与AI算力基础设施双主业发展战略，服务器贸易业务自2026年8月起实现规模化交付。 第三季度，公司实现营业收入9.21亿元，上年同期为0.14亿元；前三季度营业收入由上年同期的0.59亿元增至11.75亿元。算力侧的订单储备已在公告中可见：公司近期公告，经协商与VB客户重新签订算力服务协议及补充协议，协议总金额上涨至33.57亿元；此前的半年报披露，公司累计落地超154亿元长期算力、存储框架合同；据投资者关系活动记录，公司今年已公告披露算力及存储相关订单合计规模约183.16亿元。需要提示的是，公司在三季报中自述业务模式发生重大变化，其同比、环比数据的可比性需结合重整背景甄别。 其余公司的单季改善各有来路。同花顺在三季报中将增长归因于增值电信业务及广告与互联网推广业务等收入增加，公司第三季度归母净利润10.85亿元，环比增长55%。凯莱英第三季度归母净利润3.32亿元，环比增长约53%。公司在三季报中预计第四季度交付规模较第三季度将大幅增加、2026年全年营业收入增长19%至22%。山东玻纤的三季报将增长归因于玻纤纱价格同比上涨、销量同比增加，公司前三季度归母净利润5839.72万元，同比扭亏为盈。 除此之外，华盛昌在三季报中未披露具体的业绩变动原因。公司第三季度归母净利润1.60亿元、环比增长179%。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 10月23日会员早报：沙特阿美总部紧急疏散 巴克莱因AI裁员5000人
articles.summary: 1、【沙特阿美总部紧急疏散】10月22日，沙特国有石油巨头沙特阿美要求员工撤离位于达兰的总部、改为远程办公。六名知情人士透露，这是伊朗战争爆发以来，阿美第一次疏散总部。疏散前，总部曾响起警报，就连仍在岗的关键岗位员工也被要求居家办公，直至另行通知，阿美方面暂未回应。达兰位于沙特波斯湾沿岸，是沙特石油经济的心脏。达兰总部不只是一栋写字楼——阿美在这里设有运营中心，陆上和海上钻井平台、炼厂、出口码头以及数千公里输油管道都靠它统筹。 2、【巴克莱因AI裁员5000人】10月22日，巴克莱在发布三季报时宣布，今年将削减约5000个岗位，约占员工总数的5%（截至2025年底，巴克莱全球员工约9.3万人）；其中约1000个已在上半年裁撤，其余在年底前完成，约六成落在后台支持部门，开发人员也在其中。巴克莱在业绩材料里把这轮裁员归因于组织精简，以及AI带来的技术改造和效率提升。 3、【美国上周初请失业救济人数创三个月新低】美国劳工部周四公布，截至10月17日当周，初请失业救济人数减少6000人至19.4万，低于彭博调查经济学家预期的20万，前一周数据则从19.9万上修至20万。这是7月中旬以来的最低水平，当时初请一度降到18.9万，创下1969年以来的单周最低。用来平滑单周波动的四周移动均值降至19.775万，为2022年以来最低，几乎贴着1969年以来的最低水平。 4、【莫德纳盘中暴跌26%】美东时间10月22日（周四），莫德纳与同为美国药企的默沙东联合开发的个体化癌症疫苗，三期临床数据提前泄露，莫德纳股价盘中一度暴跌26%，创下上市以来最大盘中跌幅，收盘跌17.6%，报202.63美元；默沙东盘中一度跌近4%。这份数据原定于本周六（10月24日）在马德里召开的欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会上首次公布。泄露发生在当天午后：一家医学资讯网站抢先刊出部分结果，不久即撤下，截图却已在社交媒体上传开。ESMO随即通知记者，既然数据已经公开，便提前放出摘要，并解除全部数据的新闻禁发，两家公司当天下午也发布了新闻稿。 5、【消息称马斯克10亿美元入股好莱坞新巨头天舞】天舞本月才刚诞生，背后是一场近一年的拉锯。10月6日，派拉蒙天舞以每股31美元现金完成对华纳兄弟探索的收购，交易企业价值约1100亿美元——此前它先在竞购战中击败奈飞，又与起诉阻止交易的12个州达成和解。合并后的公司更名为天舞，股票代码由PSKY改为SKYD、转到纽交所交易，由拉里·埃里森之子大卫·埃里森出任董事长兼CEO，旗下囊括派拉蒙和华纳兄弟两大制片厂、Paramount+和HBO Max两个流媒体平台，以及CBS和CNN两家新闻机构。

articles.title: 沙特遇袭推油价破110美元，黄金失守4050美元进入“投降阶段”
articles.summary: 中东局势升温叠加美联储会议临近，金价跌至逾两个月低点。 周四现货金价暴跌2.8%，跌破每盎司4050美元关口。 与此同时，布伦特原油价格在沙特阿拉伯遭受致命袭击后飙升逾4%，突破每桶113美元。美国已下令驻沙特部分使馆人员及其家属离境，市场对地区局势进一步升级的担忧显著加剧。 能源价格高企推升通胀预期，市场正密切关注美联储下周政策会议的走向。 作为不产生利息收益的资产，黄金在高利率环境下承受持续压力。DNCA Finance投资组合经理Alex Carrier表示： 贵金属当前正经历一轮投降式抛售，波动性可能至少在下周美联储会议之前维持高位。 沙特遇袭点燃供应担忧，油价突破113美元 华尔街见闻提及 ，据CCTV国际时讯，10月22日也门胡塞武装发言人叶海亚·萨雷亚发表视频声明称，胡塞武装在过去48小时内对沙特实施了4次军事行动，使用了数枚弹道导弹和无人机。 无人机袭击沙特阿美Shaybah油田致两人死亡，但油田运营未受影响；达曼法赫德国王国际机场遭袭并出现人员伤亡。也门胡塞武装宣称过去48小时内还对沙特延布港发动了袭击。 与此同时，美国已下令部分驻沙特大使馆人员及其家属撤离，进一步显示该地区安全风险已显著上升，并可能持续恶化。 布伦特原油期货周四早盘走高，随后涨幅持续扩大至4%，创约两周内最大单日涨幅。美国WTI原油上涨2.3%，报99.37美元/桶。 油价高企令美联储货币政策路径趋于复杂 油价飙升强化了通胀持续高企的预期，进而推动各国央行收紧货币政策，而利率走高则直接压缩黄金的相对吸引力。 美联储主席Kevin Warsh上周五的表态未能打消市场对下周维持利率不变的预期，利率互换所隐含的加息25个基点的概率目前不足10%。住房开工数据走低及待售房屋销量创历史新低，亦支持按兵不动的判断。 然而，能源价格的持续攀升可能改变这一格局。当前通胀水平仍大幅高于美联储2%的目标，高能源成本令市场对年底前再次加息的预期升温——交易员目前普遍预计12月会议将再度出台加息举措。 截至周四美股收盘时段，现货金价报每盎司4028美元，较前日跳水近3%；白银跌幅更为显著，下滑4.9%至每盎司55.16美元；铂金与钯金亦同步走低。彭博美元现货指数基本持平。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 莫德纳一度大跌26%，创单日跌幅纪录！黑色素瘤疫苗数据提前泄露，结果不及预期
articles.summary: 莫德纳与默克联合研发的个性化黑色素瘤疫苗三期临床试验数据意外提前泄露，结果未达市场预期 ，引发莫德纳股价大幅下挫。此次数据披露事件不仅打压了投资者情绪，也对外界长期以来对mRNA癌症疗法的乐观预期构成考验。 周四，莫德纳股价盘中一度暴跌26%，创下单日跌幅历史纪录，后股价有所反弹，最终收跌17.6%；默克股价收跌1.8%。截至周四收盘，莫德纳股价年内依然上涨655%。 数据显示， 该疫苗可将癌症复发风险降低42%，并将远处转移（即肿瘤扩散至远端器官）风险降低38%。 这一结果低于部分投资者的预期，市场此前已对该疗法寄予厚望。 据悉，上述数据原定于本周六在马德里举行的欧洲肿瘤学会（ESMO）年会上正式发布，但相关信息提前经由社交媒体平台X上的未经核实账户流出，引发市场恐慌性抛售。默克与莫德纳随后确认，将正式公布这项名为INTerpath-001的三期临床试验完整结果。 数据提前泄露，市场措手不及 此次数据泄露事件起源于X平台上的多个未经验证账号，其中一个账号发布了一份署名Oncology Central的报告，详细披露了试验结果，但报告中所附网址链接并无法正常访问。 消息一经扩散，莫德纳与默克股价随即承压下行，此后两家公司才相继确认数据泄露属实。 疫苗正式名称为intismeran autogene，与默克的重磅肿瘤免疫药物Keytruda联合使用。 该试验共纳入逾1100名患者，受试者均为黑色素瘤手术切除后复发风险较高的人群，在接受联合治疗的同时，与仅使用Keytruda的对照组进行比较。 结果低于早期数据，分析师态度审慎 此次正式三期数据未能达到投资者此前参照的更高基准。 此前一项涉及不同患者群体、不同观察周期的早期研究——因设计差异，两者并不构成直接可比—— 显示该联合疗法可将复发或死亡风险降低49%，并将远处转移或死亡风险降低59%。 TD Cowen分析师Tyler Van Buren在泄露消息获得官方确认之前便发布客户报告指出，新数据中显示该疗法预防远处转移的效果"并不突出"，不及其在降低复发率方面的表现。他同时表示，需要进一步的详细信息才能对整体结果作出完整评估。 今年8月，莫德纳与默克曾宣布该个性化疫苗在降低致命性肿瘤复发率方面取得"显著且具有临床意义"的积极成果，成为mRNA癌症疗法史上首个三期试验成功案例，消息一出令莫德纳股价大幅飙升。 彼时两家公司并未披露具体数据，此番数据落地后，与市场想象之间的落差成为股价下挫的直接诱因。 mRNA癌症疫苗前景依然受关注，多癌种试验持续推进 尽管短期数据令市场失望，但研究人员与肿瘤学界对mRNA癌症疫苗的长期潜力仍保持关注。 数十年来，癌症疫苗研发屡遭挫折，此次三期试验的成功落地仍具有里程碑意义。 目前，莫德纳与默克正就这一个性化疫苗平台开展多项癌种扩展研究，包括肺癌、膀胱癌及其他肿瘤类型的临床试验。 该技术因能够针对个体肿瘤基因特征定制疫苗，被业界视为具备广泛应用潜力的下一代肿瘤治疗方向。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 10年期美债收益率跌回5.00%，AI资本开支退潮成债市"另类量化宽松"
articles.summary: AI概念股的一轮集中抛售，意外成为美国国债市场的最大利好。 周四，随着多家科技巨头财报引发市场对AI资本支出可持续性的质疑，美债收益率全线大幅回落，2年期至10年期美债收益率单日降幅均超15个基点，创逾一年来最大单日跌幅，美债由此迎来2025年8月以来最佳单日表现。 10年期美债收益率跌破5%，为近一个月以来首次。 高盛Rich Privorotsky在给机构客户的晨报中将这一现象定性为"令人瞩目的反身性"—— AI资本支出的每一分回撤，都意味着潜在债券供给的减少，从而直接为债市减压。 在Privorotsky看来，当超大规模云计算企业发行债务的规模已可与美国国债相提并论时，AI资本支出的任何收缩，实质上等同于减少债券市场的潜在供给压力，其效果近似于一次量化宽松。 财报触发抛售，多重信号动摇市场信心 本轮科技股下跌的导火索，来自一系列参差不齐的财报信号。据高盛Privorotsky梳理，市场承压源于至少五个因素。 其一 ，Lam Research（LRCX）业绩虽强，但未能突破市场的隐性预期上限，指引亦未提供明显上行空间，日本东京电子股价随之下跌逾6.99%； 其二 ，特斯拉将全年资本支出指引从逾250亿美元下调至约200亿美元，与SpaceX此前释放的积极信号明显背离，市场对资本支出倒退的反应尤为敏感； 其三 ，Meta财报整体表现尚可，将全年资本支出指引下限上调至1350亿美元，但这意味着仅第四季度单季支出即需达到490亿至590亿美元，规模之大引发市场对执行可行性的疑虑； 其四 ，德州仪器业绩表现优异，模拟芯片全面复苏、数据中心需求强劲，但股价反应平淡； 其五 ，DeepSeek开源推理模型DeepInfer宣称可在现有算力基础上大幅提升推理效率，从而释放存量算力，引发市场重新审视增量算力需求的必要性。 Privorotsky的总结是： 上述任何一条单独来看都算不上颠覆性，但叠加在一起，足以动摇本已脆弱的市场情绪。 他指出，在周三小幅反弹之前，半导体板块此前11个交易日中已有10日收跌，而那次反弹"表现已属乏力"。 高盛Prime数据显示，AI相关资产净敞口占全球总净敞口的比例，已从今年夏季约31%的峰值回落至约25%，多空比率从逾4.2压缩至约3.2。 受上述消息拖累，周四费城半导体指数跌超7%。英特尔、AMD跌超8%，高通跌超3%。 AI资本支出与债务供给的内在关联 Privorotsky的分析触及了一个更深层的市场结构逻辑：AI资本支出的规模，已直接影响债券市场的供需平衡。 Meta的案例颇具说明意义。仅第三季度，Meta就新增了760亿美元的表外承诺（主要为租赁负债），使表外承诺总额升至7470亿美元。 与此同时，Meta已与亚马逊一道加入自由现金流为负的阵营。Meta首席财务官在财报电话会议上警告称，"大规模投入"将推高服务成本，此言一出，Meta股价随即回吐盘后大部分涨幅。 在Privorotsky看来，当超大规模云计算企业发行债务的规模已可与美国国债相提并论时，AI资本支出的任何收缩，实质上等同于减少债券市场的潜在供给压力，其效果近似于一次量化宽松。 他由此得出一个令股票多头不安的推论： 若利率问题只能在AI股票下跌时才能缓解，债市事实上在客观上"受益于"AI交易的持续低迷，而正忙于加息的美联储也不会主动介入救市。 美债多重利好共振，期权成本飙升 除AI股票抛售外，法国主权债务危机的持续发酵也为美债提供了额外支撑。 法国10年期国债收益率与德国同期限国债收益率之差一度扩大至逾170个基点，创2011年欧债危机以来最高水平，叠加法国国内生活成本抗议浪潮， 引发资金向美债和德债避险。 此外，市场对美联储明年加息的预期也有所收敛，目前完全定价于明年1月加息25个基点，而非此前预计的12月。 上述背景下，周四美债期权对冲成本飙升至3月以来最高水平，10年期美债收益率跌破5%后，有交易员斥资约700万美元的期权费，建立10年期收益率在一个月内降至4.6%附近的头寸，合约规模约6.5万张。 与此同时，CME数据显示，长债期货出现大规模新增空头头寸，相关空头在美债上涨过程中面临被动回补压力，进一步助推涨势。 尽管布伦特原油在沙特遭受袭击后重上每桶112美元，但在花旗利率衍生品策略师Michael Chang看来： 美债正在表现出真正的避险资产属性，这对利率市场而言是令人鼓舞的信号。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
